why: Every RED the completeness oracle (frontend/roslyn/OwnSharp.Oracle) is EXPECTED to raise, tied to a finding classified by docs/notes/p037-formal-kernel.md §10.1. An input absent from expected_red must be RED-free; an input present must raise exactly these kinds and counts. A finding closes only by a ruling or a separately classified change that removes its RED, and the entry with it.

F-MEMBER.title: member bodies the legacy pass never visits: expression-bodied members, methods of struct and record types, property accessors
F-MEMBER.evidence: Program.cs enumerates ClassDeclarationSyntax only and, inside it, BaseMethodDeclarationSyntax with a block Body; the three A2.2-3P admission gates sit inside that loop, so these members reach neither functions[] nor guarded_functions[]. Witnessed by the probe (Box.op_Implicit, an expression-bodied conversion operator) and by four hostile cases.
F-MEMBER.status: open: a census finding; carrying these members in the orphan carrier is a production change to be classified on its own

F-SHADOW.title: the guarded-fact handle set is keyed by spelling, not by symbol
F-SHADOW.evidence: BuildGuardedFacts receives the legacy candidate NAMES and tests `handles.Contains(lr.Local.Name)`; the candidate collector descends into lambda bodies. Two locals spelled alike in sibling scopes, or a lambda-local creation beside an unrelated local of the same spelling, produce a var fact on a symbol that is no candidate: a false raw fact. Witnessed by three hostile cases.
F-SHADOW.status: open: an implementation defect in the A2 classifier, to be repaired as its own classified change

F-PARAMS-ELEMENT.title: an expanded params element is classified from its bare syntax
F-PARAMS-ELEMENT.evidence: For an expanded params argument the argument operation carries the call's own syntax, so the span-containment match finds nothing and the fallback classifies `model.GetOperation(expression)` of the element alone. A transparent wrapper (parentheses, the null-forgiving `!`) has no operation of its own, so the handle under it is lost and the call is not relevant; a boxing or user-defined element conversion sits on the array element, not on the expression, so a struct handle boxed into `params object[]` or a handle passed through op_Implicit into `params Box[]` yields an opaque-and-relevant slot although nothing of the handle reaches the callee. Witnessed by the hostile cases whose binding is `params` and whose value-flow shape is parens, bang, boxing or user_implicit; casts, `as` and the may-value forms have operations of their own and are classified correctly.
F-PARAMS-ELEMENT.status: open: an implementation defect in the A2 classifier, to be repaired as its own classified change

F-CONDITIONAL-RECEIVER.title: a reduced extension receiver under `?.` is not bound to ordinal 0
F-CONDITIONAL-RECEIVER.evidence: The invocation loop reads the receiver only from a MemberAccessExpressionSyntax; `r?.Ext(...)` invokes through a MemberBindingExpressionSyntax and the receiver handle is dropped, so the call is not relevant unless another argument is a handle. Witnessed by the hostile case ext-conditional-access.
F-CONDITIONAL-RECEIVER.status: open: an implementation defect in the A2 classifier, to be repaired as its own classified change

F-VOCAB.title: argument shapes the frozen vocabulary has no name for: a tested operand, an interpolation hole, an indexer argument, a constructor-initializer argument
F-VOCAB.evidence: Each is a candidate occurrence under a call-related syntax site that no frozen exclusion names; production emits no fact for any of them (correctly: no handle reaches a callee of the vocabulary), so each needs a name, never a bucket. Witnessed by four hostile cases.
F-VOCAB.status: open: awaiting a naming ruling (§10.6.4 additions)
